title: Triple equals

blocks.md:
## `===` does not convert

`0 == ""` is true because `==` coerces. `0 === ""` is false. A signal of `0` (off) is not the same as a missing name `""`.

Prefer `===` and `!==` unless you can name the coercion you want. Print whether `0` and `""` are **not** strictly equal (`true`).

blocks.promptMd: > Print `true` because `0` and `""` are not strictly equal. Use `!==` or `===`.

hintLadder.md: The starter uses `==`, which converts before it compares. That is the habit this lesson removes.
`===` and `!==` compare kind and value together, so `0 === ""` is false.
`function same(a, b) { return a === b }` answers "the same"; you want the opposite of that.

description: Strict equality compares value and kind. Loose equality will surprise you.
